<description>
The Tor password was sent as a `QuotedString` with only double quotes escaped; as Tor interprets backslash escapes inside it, any password containing a backslash was mangled (or left the string unterminated).

The Tor Control spec deliberately allows the token to be sent as unquoted hex "to avoid escaping issues", as the `SAFECOOKIE` response already is. This patch does the same for the password, and also adds a functional test covering backslashes and quotes.
</description>

diff --git a/src/torcontrol.cpp b/src/torcontrol.cpp
index 4e590ffc18..28a2fa295e 100644
--- a/src/torcontrol.cpp
+++ b/src/torcontrol.cpp
@@ -38,7 +38,6 @@
 #include <utility>
 #include <vector>
 
-using util::ReplaceAll;
 using util::SplitString;
 using util::ToString;
 
@@ -658,14 +657,14 @@ void TorController::protocolinfo_cb(TorControlConnection& _conn, const TorContro
         // Prefer NULL, otherwise SAFECOOKIE. If a password is provided, use HASHEDPASSWORD
         /* Authentication:
          *   cookie:   hex-encoded ~/.tor/control_auth_cookie
-         *   password: "password"
+         *   password: hex-encoded password
          */
         std::string torpassword = gArgs.GetArg("-torpassword", "");
         if (!torpassword.empty()) {
             if (methods.contains("HASHEDPASSWORD")) {
                 LogDebug(BCLog::TOR, "Using HASHEDPASSWORD authentication");
-                ReplaceAll(torpassword, "\"", "\\\"");
-                _conn.Command("AUTHENTICATE \"" + torpassword + "\"", std::bind_front(&TorController::auth_cb, this));
+                // Send the password hex-encoded rather than as a QuotedString, so it never needs escaping.
+                _conn.Command("AUTHENTICATE " + HexStr(torpassword), std::bind_front(&TorController::auth_cb, this));
             } else {
                 LogWarning("tor: Password provided with -torpassword, but HASHEDPASSWORD authentication is not available");
             }
diff --git a/test/functional/feature_torcontrol.py b/test/functional/feature_torcontrol.py
index bba021739e..47701b0178 100755
--- a/test/functional/feature_torcontrol.py
+++ b/test/functional/feature_torcontrol.py
@@ -112,13 +112,13 @@ class TorControlTest(BitcoinTestFramework):
         self._port_counter = getattr(self, '_port_counter', 0) + 1
         return p2p_port(self.num_nodes + self._port_counter)
 
-    def restart_with_mock(self, mock_tor):
+    def restart_with_mock(self, mock_tor, extra_args=None):
         mock_tor.start()
         self.restart_node(0, extra_args=[
             f"-torcontrol=127.0.0.1:{mock_tor.port}",
             "-listenonion=1",
             "-debug=tor",
-        ])
+        ] + (extra_args or []))
 
         # Wait for connection and PROTOCOLINFO command
         mock_tor.conn_ready.wait(timeout=10)
@@ -186,6 +186,42 @@ class TorControlTest(BitcoinTestFramework):
         # Clean up
         mock_tor.stop()
 
+    def test_password_auth(self):
+        self.log.info("Test that -torpassword is sent hex-encoded, so special characters survive")
+
+        class HashedPasswordServer(MockTorControlServer):
+            def __init__(self, port, expected_password):
+                self.expected_hex = expected_password.encode().hex()
+                super().__init__(port)
+
+            def _get_response(self, command):
+                if command == "PROTOCOLINFO 1":
+                    return (
+                        "250-PROTOCOLINFO 1\r\n"
+                        "250-AUTH METHODS=HASHEDPASSWORD\r\n"
+                        "250-VERSION Tor=\"0.1.2.3\"\r\n"
+                        "250 OK\r\n"
+                    )
+                elif command.startswith("AUTHENTICATE "):
+                    sent_hex = command.removeprefix("AUTHENTICATE ")
+                    if sent_hex != self.expected_hex:
+                        return "515 Bad authentication\r\n"
+                    return "250 OK\r\n"
+                return super()._get_response(command)
+
+        password = 'pa\\ss"word\\'
+        mock_tor = HashedPasswordServer(self.next_port(), password)
+        self.restart_with_mock(mock_tor, extra_args=[f"-torpassword={password}"])
+
+        self.wait_until(lambda: len(mock_tor.received_commands) >= 2, timeout=10)
+        assert_equal(mock_tor.received_commands[1], f"AUTHENTICATE {password.encode().hex()}")
+
+        # Authentication succeeded, so the node goes on to create the onion service
+        self.wait_until(lambda: any(c.startswith("ADD_ONION ") for c in mock_tor.received_commands), timeout=10)
+
+        # Clean up
+        mock_tor.stop()
+
     def test_pow_fallback(self):
         self.log.info("Test that ADD_ONION retries without PoW on 512 error")
 
@@ -274,6 +310,7 @@ class TorControlTest(BitcoinTestFramework):
     def run_test(self):
         self.test_basic()
         self.test_partial_data()
+        self.test_password_auth()
         self.test_pow_fallback()
         self.test_oversized_line()
         self.test_overmany_lines()
